01What is art therapy

Art therapy is an integrative mental health profession. A credentialed art therapist uses the creative process, psychological theory, and the brain–body relationship to help people work through trauma, grief, identity, anxiety, and change.

It is not an art class. It is led by a master’s-level, credentialed clinician.

No art experience is needed, and there is no wrong way to make. Art therapy meets people of every age, background, and ability — and works alongside how each person communicates.

The creative process is the work.

03Advocacy & licensure

Indiana is ready to make art therapy official.

Art therapists already work in hospitals, schools, clinics, and communities across the state. Licensure would name the profession Indiana already relies on — protecting the public, and opening access to care that many people cannot reach today.

01Protect the public +

Without a license, anyone can call themselves an art therapist. Licensure ties the title to training, ethics, and accountability, so people know who is qualified.

02Open access to care +

State recognition opens pathways to insurance and Medicaid reimbursement, so more Hoosiers reach care, including communities underserved today.

03Match credential to work +

Art therapists train at the master’s level and hold national ATCB credentials, yet practice under a borrowed license. Recognition names the profession for what it is.

04Beyond the statehouse +

Recognition reaches hospitals, schools, and communities, where art therapists are counted, hired, and trusted as the clinicians they are.

Where things stand

No art therapy license in Indiana yet

Art therapists practice as Licensed Mental Health Counselors (LMHC) and hold national ATCB credentials (ATR-P, ATR, ATR-BC).

  • Licensure bills introduced across several sessions (HB 1239, SB 317, and others)
  • Goals: independent licensure, title protection, Medicaid reimbursement
  • Bills not yet heard in committee
  • Ohio passed licensure in 2023; Nebraska in 2024
